differences.title: 1. SANDBOXING
differences.leftDesc: WebAssembly runs in a secure, sandboxed virtual machine with restricted capabilities, preventing unauthorized access to host system resources and ensuring memory safety.
differences.rightDesc: Containers use OS kernel features like namespaces and cgroups for isolation, sharing the host kernel but restricting access to processes, networks, and file systems.

differences.title: 2. PORTABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Wasm binaries can run identically across any platform with a compatible runtime, abstracting away underlying hardware and operating system specifics for true universal compatibility.
differences.rightDesc: Containers are typically built for and run on a specific host OS (e.g., Linux containers on Linux). Cross-OS compatibility often requires emulation or specialized layers.

differences.title: 3. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Wasm is designed for efficient compilation and execution, often achieving performance close to native code with minimal runtime overhead, ideal for compute-intensive tasks.
differences.rightDesc: Containers have some performance overhead due to the OS kernel interactions and resource management, though generally much less than full VMs.

differences.title: 4. RESOURCE CONSUMPTION
differences.leftDesc: Wasm modules are typically small and require minimal memory and CPU, making them efficient for edge computing, IoT, and browser-based applications with limited resources.
differences.rightDesc: Containers, while lighter than VMs, still package an OS user-space and libraries, leading to larger image sizes and higher baseline resource usage.

differences.title: 5. SECURITY MODEL
differences.leftDesc: WebAssembly explicitly defines capabilities required for operations. Any action not permitted by the sandbox or explicitly granted is denied, providing a granular security approach.
differences.rightDesc: Container security relies on Linux kernel features and configured permissions. Misconfigurations or kernel vulnerabilities can potentially expose the host system.

differences.title: 6. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Excellent for running complex computations (graphics, ML, crypto) securely within browsers or as plugins, extending web capabilities with near-native performance.
differences.rightDesc: Ideal for packaging and deploying applications consistently across different environments, managing services, and enabling microservices architectures at scale.

differences.title: 7. PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES
differences.leftDesc: Many languages (C++, Rust, Go, C#) can compile to Wasm, enabling code reuse and execution in environments where native compilation is not feasible or desired.
differences.rightDesc: Primarily designed for languages that compile directly to machine code for the host OS, like Go, Java, Python (with interpreters), and compiled languages like C++.
